uncited: This method implements a single-stage vertex shader for splat rasterization that integrates deferred indirect lighting (IBL) and depth-based occlusion directly into the vertex processing stage, rather than deferring these calculations to the fragment shader.
It solves the problem of efficiently rendering large-scale Gaussian splats with physically-based relighting and AR scene occlusion on Metal GPUs.

It differs from standard splatting by performing lighting and occlusion checks per-vertex (or per-primitive) to modulate coverage and color before fragment generation, reducing fragment shader workload and enabling early discard of occluded primitives.
- **Inputs:** Instance ID, vertex ID, splat metadata (position, covariance, color, opacity), chunk metadata, uniform data (view parameters, lighting environment), scene depth map.
Apply depth occlusion: if `relight.occlusionEnabled != 0u` and scene depth $D_{scene} > 0.01$, linearize splat NDC depth to meters and compare with scene depth.
- **Time Complexity:** $O(1)$ per vertex, but includes texture lookups for IBL and depth.
- **Memory Complexity:** Depends on chunk metadata and environment maps.
Precision issues may arise in depth comparison.
This method is part of the MetalGaussianSplatRelighting project, an unofficial implementation for rendering Gaussian splats with relighting on Metal GPUs.
It was developed to integrate physically-based lighting and AR occlusion into the splatting pipeline.
